unit.title: Engineering a Tiny IR and Control-Flow Graph Analyzer
unit.scope: A bounded, manager-authored kickoff covering intermediate-representation contracts, control-flow graph construction, reachability, deterministic diagnostics, and automated tests.
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student building production-oriented software-engineering habits
prerequisites: Familiarity with at least one programming language
Ability to run a compiler, tests, and a command-line program
learning_objectives: Explain the distinct roles of source syntax, an intermediate representation, and a control-flow graph.
Turn a written input contract into a validated in-memory representation.
Construct deterministic successor and predecessor relations and compute entry reachability.
Separate parsing, validation, graph analysis, and serialization into testable components.
Use automated tests and precise diagnostics to defend boundary cases.

completion_policy.boundary: Completion can be awarded only for this kickoff unit; it is never evidence that the approximately 60-hour catalog course is complete.
unit_completion_requires: A submitted implementation and its durable test evidence
Responses to the learner-safe comprehension prompts
Promotion by a validator controlled by the worker harness
completion_policy.expansion_rule: Later jobs must verify materials, author and validate additional units, and add explicit dependency edges before making broader progress claims.
